{"search_note":"Overall: mixed positive, but mostly macro-structural rather than sector-specific. Sharif’s 2024 agenda clearly pushed fiscal/market reforms and some state-capacity cleanup, but I found little direct evidence of big, clearly attributable 2024 investments in schools, hospitals, roads, or digital capacity. The strongest evidence is about predictable regulation, public-finance discipline, and SOE reform.

Search gap:
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a major, Sharif-attributed package for schools, universities, primary healthcare, roads, ports, broadband rollout, or civil-service modernization with measurable implementation.
- The available evidence is mostly about macro reform, SOE privatization, tariff correction, and investment climate repair, which matter for productivity but are not the same as direct infrastructure or human-capital investment.","evidence":[{"title":"Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-07-12","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-extended-fund-eff","summary":"Claim: the program called for broadening the tax base, improving SOE management, strengthening competition, securing a level playing field, phasing out distortive incentives, and advancing governance/anti-corruption reforms. This is strong evidence of an attempt to build more predictable, productivity-friendly rules, even if it is still program language rather than completed delivery.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3","5B.5"]},{"title":"Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-05-10","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741","summary":"Claim: the IMF said sustainable recovery required strict fiscal targets, a market-determined exchange rate, better tax collection, SOE reform, governance/anti-corruption measures, and continued support for inclusive growth and job creation. This supports a productivity-foundations reading, especially on administrative capacity and regulation, but it also shows how much remained unfinished.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3","5B.5"]},{"title":"IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation for Pakistan and Approves 37-month Extended Arrangement","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-09-27","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr","summary":"Claim: the new program aimed to entrench macro stability, strengthen competition, remove state distortions, improve the FDI regime, reform SOEs, and support a fairer business environment. This is concrete pro-productivity evidence because it reduces state distortion and can improve investment conditions.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3","5B.5"]},{"title":"Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says","publisher":"Reuters via Dawn","date":"2024-10-10","url":"https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298","summary":"Claim: the government renegotiated power-purchase contracts to cut electricity tariffs and save about Rs60 billion a year. This is indirect but relevant evidence for administrative capacity and rule predictability in the economic portfolio.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.2","5B.3"]},{"title":"Pakistan Finance Division profile: Muhammad Aurangzeb","publisher":"Government of Pakistan, Finance Division","date":"2024-03","url":"https://finance.gov.pk/profile_minister.html","summary":"Claim: the ministry described Aurangzeb as a long-time international banker whose mandate was sustainable macro stability and prudent, transparent public financial management. This is positive evidence for administrative capacity and consultation-based policymaking, though the arrangement remained PM-led.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.2"]},{"title":"Pakistan 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-10-10","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152","summary":"Claim: Pakistan still had a narrow tax base, weak governance, an outsized state role, and a business environment that hindered investment. That is negative evidence that the productivity foundations were not yet secure.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3"]},{"title":"Pakistan 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024-09-27","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr","summary":"Claim: the IMF also said investment remained very low and the state remained too large in the economy, so the fair-rules and productivity agenda was real but still unfinished.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.4","5B.3"]},{"title":"Pakistan: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-10-10","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank","summary":"Claim: growth had recovered, but poverty still rose. That weakens any claim that 2024 visibly improved broad productivity foundations in a way that had already reached households.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.3"]}]}
